messages.text: Masters, Webb criticise FIFA over Balogun red card controversy

metadata.summary: Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban.
metadata.content: Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup USA striker Folarin Balogun had a red card suspended at the World Cup; it caused huge controversy after Donald Trump had called Gianni Infantino ahead of the last 32 match against Belgium; Balogun was sent off against Bosnia & Herzegovina and was suspended for two games Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Wednesday 19 August 2026 18:01, UK Image: Folarin Balogun was sent off against Bosnia & Herzegovina - but had his two-game ban controversially suspended Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban. Richard Masters , the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb , the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game. Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced. messages.text: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory

metadata.summary: Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively.
metadata.content: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory We were treated to another epic renewal of the Juddmonte International on Wednesday but it was far from the match-race that it was built up to be, with Item delivered late to deny Almaqam in a thrilling finish to the York feature. Wednesday 19 August 2026 17:00, UK Image: Item ridden by Colin Keane on their way to winning the Juddmonte International Stakes Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively. Hawk Mountain rather unexpectedly set the early pace, with stablemate Constitution River tucked in keenly behind him and odds-on favourite Ombudsman at the rear under William Buick, kept company by another Aidan O'Brien runner, Action. Hawk Mountain was still in front as they moved to the top of the long Knavesmire straight, with Buick beginning to make headway on the inside rail, as Ryan Moore and Constitution River kicked for home over two furlongs out. Ombudsman kept making ground on the inside, but the dangers were coming on the outside and it was Ed Walker's Almaqam who pulled away with half a furlong to run, only for Item to arrive in full flight, just getting his head down on the line in the hands of Colin Keane.
